content.user_title: Build an Academic CV for Your Next Application
content.value_statement: Academic applications need a clear record of research, teaching, and service. This skill organizes your supplied achievements into a CV tailored to academic roles.
actual_capabilities: Recommend CV section order for faculty, postdoctoral, lecturer, and research scientist applications.
Format education and academic appointments with dates, advisors, and dissertation details.
Organize publications by type and status, with author emphasis and available DOIs.
Structure grants by funding status, role, project dates, and award amounts.
Organize teaching, mentoring, service, presentations, memberships, and awards.
Provide Markdown CV sections, discipline-specific formatting notes, and a checklist of missing information.
limitations: The skill supplies writing guidance, not automated PDF, Word, or LaTeX export.
It does not independently verify publications, grant awards, credentials, or citation metadata.
Disciplinary guidance is general and may differ from institutional requirements.
Complete entries depend on the accuracy and detail of your supplied records.

use_cases.title: Prepare a postdoctoral application
use_cases.description: Organize doctoral research, publications, presentations, and fellowships into a research-focused CV.

use_cases.title: Update a faculty CV
use_cases.description: Integrate new publications, funding, mentoring, and service into a comprehensive academic record.

use_cases.title: Prioritize teaching experience
use_cases.description: Place courses, curriculum development, mentoring, and teaching awards prominently for lecturer applications.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic academic CV
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an academic CV outline for a [career stage] in [discipline]. Use these records: [education and experience]. List missing information separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Build an initial structure from basic records.

prompt_templates.title: Organize publications and funding
prompt_templates.prompt: Format these publications and grants for my [discipline] CV: [records]. Separate publication and funding statuses. Preserve supplied author order, dates, and amounts.

prompt_templates.title: Tailor a CV to an academic role
prompt_templates.prompt: Tailor my CV for a [role] in [discipline]. Use [CV] and [position requirements]. Recommend section order and format relevant achievements without inventing facts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Align an existing CV with a specific application.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare research and teaching variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [CV records], prepare research-focused and teaching-focused CV structures. Explain section priorities, preserve all supplied facts, and list unresolved details for each version.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Adapt one academic record for different appointment types.

output_examples.input: A doctoral candidate supplies education, two published articles, and teaching assistant experience for a biology postdoctoral application.
output: Recommended order: Contact Information, Education, Research Experience, Publications, Presentations, Teaching Experience, Awards, Service.
Publication sections distinguish peer-reviewed articles from work under review or in preparation.
Items to add: Dissertation title, advisor name, article DOIs, and research appointment dates.

output_examples.input: A lecturer applicant supplies a record of introductory courses, curriculum development, mentoring, and publications.
output: Recommended order: Contact Information, Education, Teaching Experience, Course Development, Mentoring, Publications, Service, Awards.
Teaching entries include course titles, instructor roles, institutions, dates, and enrollment when supplied.
Items to add: Missing course numbers, teaching evaluation summaries, and mentoring dates.

best_practices: Provide accurate dates, publication statuses, author order, funding roles, and award amounts before requesting formatting.
Specify your discipline, career stage, target role, and any institutional CV requirements.
Review every entry and resolve missing details before submitting the final CV.
anti_patterns: Do not present example credentials, publications, or grant amounts as your own achievements.
Do not combine published, pending, and proposed work without clear status labels.
Do not apply one section order or page limit to every academic role.

faq.question: How is an academic CV different from a resume?
faq.answer: An academic CV records scholarship, teaching, and service comprehensively. A resume usually highlights selected experience within a shorter format.

faq.question: Which academic roles does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for tenure-track faculty, postdoctoral researchers, lecturers, teaching faculty, and research scientists.

faq.question: Can it format publications and grants?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides publication categories and grant formats covering status, roles, dates, and amounts from your supplied records.

faq.question: Does it verify my achievements?
faq.answer: No. You must verify credentials, publication details, grant amounts, and other claims before submission.

faq.question: Can it export a finished PDF or Word document?
faq.answer: The skill specifies Markdown output and formatting guidance. It does not include document export tools.

faq.question: How long should my CV be?
faq.answer: Length depends on career stage and application requirements. The guidance suggests roughly two to four pages for graduate students and longer records for faculty.
